title: Funnel Cake with Sugar and Fruit

content.title: About
content.content: Funnel cake is a deep‑fried batter formed into a lacy net, dusted with sugar and served with a variety of fresh fruits. The batter is typically made from flour, eggs, milk, sugar and leavening, then poured through a funnel into hot oil until golden and crisp. Sugar adds sweetness, while berries or sliced fruits bring aroma and a bright flavor contrast.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Funnel cake originated in the United States in the early 20th century and became a staple at fairs and festivals.
Traditionally the batter is poured through a funnel or squeeze bottle, creating the characteristic “mesh” pattern.
In Russia a similar treat is known as “testovoe oblako” or fried pancake‑net, but the authentic recipe retains its American roots.
Sugar is usually sprinkled immediately after frying while the cake is still hot, allowing it to melt slightly.
Common fruit toppings include strawberries, raspberries, kiwi, banana or lightly caramelized apples.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The batter provides carbohydrates and a modest amount of protein, delivering quick energy.

items.title: Vitamins from fruit
items.content: Fresh berries and fruits are rich in vitamin C, vitamin A and antioxidants that support immunity.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The cake contains potassium and magnesium, while fruit adds calcium and iron.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fruit toppings increase fiber content, aiding digestion.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Fresh fruit contributes water, helping maintain fluid balance.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can raise blood glucose levels and contribute to tooth decay.

items.title: Fried oil
items.content: Deep‑frying adds saturated fats and calories, which should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional recipes use wheat flour, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Fruit allergies
items.content: Certain fruits may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the funnel cake hot, dusted with powdered sugar and topped with fresh berries, sliced banana, kiwi or other fruits. Eat it straight away with a fork or by hand, optionally drizzling light syrup or whipped cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Funnel cake is best enjoyed immediately after frying. Leftovers can be kept in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days and reheated in the oven to restore crispness. Freezing is not recommended, as the texture deteriorates.
